headlines.text: Turning the clock back to 2023: MJF vs. Kenny Omega clashed for the AEW World Heavyweight Title, appearing on Collision, rated 9.10 ? a genuine showstealer. It was the 40th time the AEW World Heavyweight Title had been on the line, a real landmark for that championship. It marked MJF's 10th match with the title on the line. In their first-ever encounter, MJF broke Kenny Omega's 346-day reign record by retaining the AEW World Title through a Panama Sunrise and a heatseeker piledriver in a match both men later shook hands after.

That Wednesday in 2020, Kenny Omega vs. Penta El Zero M met in a Tournament Match, in the night's main event on Dynamite, rated 8.14 ? a hard-hitting, high-quality battle. A highlight-reel semifinal ? Penta stepped in as a late replacement for his injured brother Rey Fenix, and the two delivered real fireworks (including a Canadian Destroyer off the middle turnbuckle) before Omega advanced to face Hangman Page in the tournament final.
Looking back to 2022, when Matt Taven announced their arrival in style, headlining their very first AEW appearance against Wardlow, appearing on Rampage, rated 4.75.

secondaries.text: On a Saturday in 2023, back when Hikaru Shida vs. Abadon clashed for the AEW Women's World Title in a Fright Night Fight match, appearing on Collision, rated 6.25. It marked Hikaru Shida's 20th match with the title on the line.
Rewind to 2020, when AEW welcomed Leyla Hirsch for the first time against Serena Deeb, appearing on Dynamite, rated 6.39.
2020 brought us this moment: it was the first-ever encounter between Adam Page and Wardlow, opening the card on Dynamite, rated 7.19 ? a good, competitive contest.
